title: Japan Leads Geolocated Tokenized Treasury Holders but Holds 0.4% of Value
description: Chainalysis data show Japan accounts for 16.4% of geolocated tokenized Treasury holders but only 0.4% of their value, while three other markets hold 66.9% by value.
why_it_matters: The split between holder count and capital concentration shows that broader retail access does not necessarily distribute tokenized Treasury liquidity evenly across markets.
keyTakeaways: Japan leads the identifiable holder count but represents a small share of geolocated value.
Italy, Portugal and Singapore together account for 66.9% of geolocated tokenized Treasury value.
The figures cover Chainalysis's 12-month reporting period ending July 1, 2026.
body:
Chainalysis reported on October 14 that Japan represented 16.4% of identifiable tokenized U.S. Treasury holders but only 0.4% of the corresponding value. Italy accounted for 29.9% of geolocated value, Portugal for 18.8% and Singapore for 18.2%, a combined 66.9%. The United States ranked fourth by value at 10.5%.

The figures cover Chainalysis's 12-month reporting period ending July 1, 2026, rather than a current market snapshot. The firm measured $15.42 billion of tokenized U.S. Treasury value, up 125% from $6.86 billion. Chainalysis interprets the holder-value gap as evidence that a relatively small group of large foreign holders drives much of the market while a broader retail base holds smaller positions.
